full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Hassan Ameen, J : This criminal appeal, at the instance of four accused-appellagts, namely, (1) Monu Sheikh alias Manu Miah, (2) Kalu Mia, (3) Mobarak alias Muga and (4) Md. Mofiz alias Mofizuddin, is directed against the judgment and order dated 26.04.1997, passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, First Court, Mymensingh, in Sessions Case No. 37 of 1995 arising out of G.R.No. 51(2)92 corresponding to Trial P.S. Case No. 1(5)92, convicting them (appellants) under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and sentencing each of them to imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Tk. 5,000/- in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for six months more while acquitting three others co-accused from the charge. 

 2. The prosecution case, in brief, is that Abul Kashem the deceased was an Assistant Teacher of Amirabari High School and was also Chairman of Village Defence Party of Guziam and often used to try the local miscreants and punish the culprits and besides that he had enmity with villagers—Abdul Majid and Azizul over his own village landed property. The further prosecution case is that the deceased in the night following 03.05.1992 at 11'00 P.M. took his bed on taking meal after coming from Bogar Bazar and his wife, sons and daughter also took their bed in different huts of his house. The miscreants entered into the P.O. house at 00'30 hours on 04.05.1992 being armed with 'duo, 'char, torch-light and entered into the room of the deceased by breaking open the door while 4/5 miscreants were guarding the said house. The miscreants dragged the deceased from his room when his (deceased) wife, sons and daughter raised alarm, but went away with the deceased after beating them. The miscreants fastened the deceased with rope with a mango tree standing on the south-west corner of the home-stead and caused severe injuries and different parts of his (deceased) body with the aforesaid weapons. The miscreants further chopped off the head of the deceased from his body and went away leaving the dead body there. The accused Manu Dacoit, Mobarak, Mofiz, Kasu alias Kuddus, Abdul Majid and Azizul were recognized by wife, sons, and daughter of the deceased during the occurrence in the light of 'kupi-buti' of their room along with focus of torch-light of the miscreants. The informant further alleged that he and the FIR named witnesses, namely, Abul Hossain, Abdul Latif, Aminul, Manu Miah, Kadir, Matin and many men of their village who came to the place of occurrence on hearing alarm had seen the occurrence as well as recognized the miscreants. Accordingly, the FIR was lodged at 13'30 hours on 04.05.1992 i.e. twelve and half hours after the alleged occurrence whereupon the aforesaid police station case was started. 

 3. Police took up investigation, visited the place of occurrence, prepared inquest report of the dead body of deceased and sent it to morgue for holding post-mortem examination, seized alamats by preparing seizure list, prepared sketch-map of the place of occurrence with separate index thereof, examined the witnesses and recorded their statements under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and finally submitted a charge-sheet against the accused-appellants and three others under sections 458/302/34 of the Penal Code, since prima-facie case was made out against them. 

 4. The case record ultimately came to the present Trial Court who on the basis of materials available on record framed charge against the accused-appellants and three others under Sections 458/302/34 of the Penal Code and read it over to the accused on dock to which they pleaded not guilty and demanded trial. 

 6. The defence case as could be gathered from the trend of cross-examination is total denial and their inter-alia case is that the deceased was a notorious dacoit of the locality who may have been murdered by miscreants but they have been falsely implicated in this case out of enmity and grudge and that no occurrence took place on the date, time, place and in the manner as alleged. 

 7. The learned Trial Court thereafter in consideration of the evidence on record as well as facts and circumstances of the case, however found the accused-appellants guilty for the offence under Sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and as such convicted them thereunder and sentenced to imprisonment for the term as well as to pay a fine with default clause as mentioned above without passing any order about the charge so framed against the accused-appellants and others under Section 458 of the Penal Code. The learned Trial Court, however, found the rest three accused not guilty for the offence charged and as such acquitted them therefrom. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied thereby the accused-appellants have come up with the present appeal which is opposed by the respondent-State through the learned Assistant Attorney General Mr. Md. Rabiul Karim. 

 other material papers/documents as available in paper-book and submits that this is a case of no evidence, but the learned Trial Court arrived at a decision on guess and surmise. He further submits that the learned Trial Court failed to consider that the prosecution did not come with clean hand inasmuch as the means of recognition of the miscreants have not been brought on record as exhibit to show their bonafide and that inclusion of some other accused who had not been charge-sheeted clearly indicates that the present case is the out come of enmity. He further submits that the learned Trial Court failed to consider the defence case and that the independent witnesses whose names find place in the FIR having not been examined in this case, the present judgment suffers from material illegality. He lastly submits that the learned Trial Court failed to consider that the alleged occurrence took place at 00'30 hours on 04.05.1992 and that post-mortem examination took place at 09'00 A.M. on 06.05.1992 as is evident from post-mortem examination report i.e. almost fifty-six half hours after the alleged death of the deceased, but the doctor who held post-mortem examination on the dead body of deceased found rigor mortise present thereto which was held long after fifty-six and half hours of the occurrence which itself proves that the occurrence did not take place on the date as alleged and the emptiness of urinal bladder along with stomach of the deceased justify that the death of the deceased did not take place on the date, time, place and in the manner as alleged and accordingly he submits that the impugned judgment and order of conviction is liable to be set-aside.

He claimed that the same was reported by wife of the deceased when he rushed there on hearing alarm. This P.W of course, claimed that he noticed different injuries on chest as well as head of the deceased. This P.W claimed that he recognized the miscreants at the place of occurrence in the light of torch. He proved the FIR as well as the seizure list. In cross he admitted that there were 12/14 members in the P.O house including himself. He also said that the deceased had three sons, namely, Sayed, Tarek, Babu and a daughter, namely, Karuna Khatun who were in the said house in the night of occurrence. He further admitted that neighbours have got their houses by the four sides of the P.O. house and the neighbours came to the P.O house on hearing alarm in the night of occurrence. He then said that Janab Ali Fakir, Abdul Hye, Nurul Islam Master, Fazlul Hoque Master and others came there and heard the occurrence from the wife of deceased. This P.W. claimed that his brother's son Aminul Islam was with him when he rushed to the place of occurrence and that he recognized the miscreants in the light of his own 3 battery torch, but frankly admitted that he did not hand over the said torch to the Daroga during investigation. He also admitted that the accused had enmity with the deceased. He admitted that he has got no paper to show that the deceased was Chairman of local Village Defence party. He denied the defence suggestion that the deceased was a leader of local dacoits who used to commit bus dacoity near Boga Bridge situated near to their house and that his (deceased) associates murdered the deceased over division of booty so looted during bus dacoity and that no occurrence took place on the date, time, place and in the manner as alleged. He denied the defence suggestion that

She also claimed that her 'kamla' Kader knew the occurrence. He claimed that Fazlu Master, Harez, Manik, 'Kaka" Latif and Kalam along with other co-villagers came to the place of occurrence after the occurrence. He denied the defence suggestion that Helal Dacoit has murdered the deceased due to enmity. He denied the defence suggestion that the present case has been started only to harass the accused. He categorically said that he sworn an affidavit on 10.12.1992 out of fear of the accused for which he did not lodge any G.D. entry. 

 13. P.W. 4 Abul Hossain claimed that on hearing alarm he rushed to the P.O. house and found the deceased being tied with rope along with mango tree and recognized accused Manu Dacoit,.Kalu, Mobarak, Mojid, Azizul, Kuddus and Mofiz in the light of his own torch while they were going away therefrom. He also claimed that Lalu, Afaz, Seraj and others also came there. He admitted that they found the deceased being with mango tree while his head was lying in drain. He then said that on their alarm, the wife of the deceased, sons and `kamla' of the deceased came there. He denied the defence suggestion that he did not state about seeing the dead body of the deceased in the light of torch in his statement under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. He denied the defence suggestion that the deceased used to keep the looted articles and that no occurrence took place on the date as alleged. He frankly admitted that was no light at the time of occurrence and that he did not deposit the torch-light through which he recognized the miscreants to Daroga during investigation of the case. He denied the defence suggestion that the men of Helal Dacoit had murdered the deceased over division of booty. 

 14. P.W. 5 Abdul Matin another inmates of the P.O. house said about the occurrence as well as recognition of the accused. He claimed that he recognized the accused in the light of his torch but in cross frankly admitted that he did not deposit the said torch to the Daroga during investigation of the case. He denied the defence suggestion that his story of seeing the accused 

 15. P.W. 6 Aminul Islam corroborated the prosecution case about dragging out of the deceased by the accused in the night' of occurrence. He admitted that he stated in his statement under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure about seeing the occurrence personally, but in the next sentence he admitted that he stated before the Daroga that he did not see the occurrence personally, but heard from others. He denied the defence suggestion that the accused did not murder his 'Chacha'—the deceased. He further denied the defence suggestion that the deceased used to keep the looked articles and that the men of Helal Dacoit murdered the deceased over division of booty. In cross he frankly admitted that he did not state in his statement under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure that he heard the occurrence after arrival at the place of occurrence. He denied the defence suggestion that he did not see the occurrence personally. 

 16. P.W. 7 Abdul Latif brother of the deceased and P.W. 8 Fazlul Haque a neighbour have in a voice said about reporting of the occurrence by the inmates of the P.O. house. They also said about their recognition of miscreants in the light of torch. Both of them said' that besides themselves the other 40/50 neighbours who are not related to them assembled at the P.O. house after the occurrence. They denied the defence suggestion that the story of seeing of the accused with the light of torch is false. 

 19. P.Ws 13, 14 and 15 are the police officials claimed to have carried out investigation of the case. P.W. 13 in his cross-examination admitted that P.W. Tarek did not state that the accused had chopped off the head of the deceased from his body or that they (accused) caused injuries on different parts of body of the deceased. P.W. 15 claimed that he examined five P.Ws. during investigation, but none of them said that accused Manu entered into the P.O. room and caused injuries on different parts of the body of deceased nor any one said that the miscreants had dragged the deceased out of his room. This is all about the evidence on record. 

 20. The critical analysis of the evidence indicates that the prosecution proved the unnatural death of the deceased by good and satisfactory evidence and the defence never tried to dislodge this part of evidence so led by the prosecution. The doctor P.W. 12 who held post mortem examination on the dead body of deceased has also corroborated the prosecution case about unnatural death of the deceased. Now, the only question left as to whether the deceased was murdered on the date, time and place as alleged by the prosecution. The specific case of the prosecution is that the deceased took his bed at about 11.00 P.M. in the night following 03.05.1992 after taking his meal and that the occurrence took place at about 00'30 hours i.e. nearly 111/2/2hours after taking his meal. The post-mortem examination report reveals that the doctor who held the same on the dead body of deceased found the stomach and urinal bladder empty. So, there is no explanation as to how the stomach as well as urinal bladder of the deceased were empty just after l1/2/2 hours after his taking of meal. This fact raises a doubt about the time of occurrence. Further, it appears that the doctor P.W. 12 who held post-mortem examination on the dead body of the deceased found rigor mortis present. In this connection we may be permitted to mention here that according to Modi, in temperate regions, rigor mortis unusually lasts for two to three days. In Northern India, the usual duration of rigor mortis is twenty-four to forty-eight hours in winter and eighteen to thirty-six hours in summer. According to the investigation of Mackenzie in Calcutta the average duration is nineteen hours and twelve minutes, the shortest period being three hours and the longest forty hours. It may be re-called here that the alleged occurrence took place in the month of May (summer season) according to English calendar and as such the presence of rigor Mortis in the dead body of deceased so found by the doctor—P.W. 12 who held post-mortem examination thereto long after fifty-six hours of the alleged occurrence in no way justify the claim of the prosecution that the deceased was murdered in his house at 00'30 hours on 04.05.1992. Now, we may sum up the observation of the doctor—P.W. 12 who held post-mortem examination on the dead body of deceased that the death of the deceased did not take place on the date as alleged by the prosecution, because the presence of rigor mortis long after fifty-six hours of alleged time of occurrence and emptiness of stomach as well as urinal bladder just after 11/2/2 hours of taking of meal raises a suspicion about the time of death of the deceased. 

 21. Now the question is left as to whether the prosecution has been able to prove the participation of the accused-appellants in the occurrence. Admittedly the occurrence took place in the night and the persistent case of the prosecution is that the witnesses recognized the accused in the light of their respective torch as well as a 'kupi-buti' which was allegedly burning in the P.O. house, but the 'kupi-bati' though has been seized in this case, appears to have not been identified by any inmate of the P.O. house and admittedly the torch-lights by which the inmates of the P.O. house recognized the miscreants/ accused-appellants have not been brought on record as exhibits. This fact alone raises a serious doubt about the prosecution claim over means of recognition. Had the witness as referred to above recognized the accused-appellants in the light of 'kupi-bati' or their torch, those could have been brought on record during trial and the same having not been done so, we are constrained to hold that the prosecution has hopelessly failed to prove the means of recognition in this case. 

 22. Then come about the alleged behavior of the accused-appellants with the deceased. It has been alleged in the FIR. that the deceased had inimical term with the accused-appellants over landed property and that there were some cases pending over the same. The defence also admitted the same. However, there is evidence that besides the private witnesses examined in this case, the other disinterested neighbours including the chairman and member of local union Parishad came to the place of occurrence just after the occurrence, but none of them found to have been examined in this case inasmuch as all the private P.Ws. are none but admitted close relations of the deceased. In view of admitted bitter relationship between the parties as well as the private witnesses so examined in this case it was desirable for the prosecution to examine the close independent and disinterested neighbours. In the face of clear admission that 40/50 co-villagers were present just after the occurrence including the chairman and member of local union Parishad and they having not been produced in Court to show the bonafide of the prosecution, we find no other alternative but to hold that had they been examined, would not have supported the prosecution case and in view of this matter the benefit of section 114(g) of the Evidence Act should go in favour of the defence. More so, the wife, brother and son of the deceased did not dare to state on dock that they stated the names of the accused-appellants as murderers of the deceased to the Daroga while they were examined under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. So, in all fairness, it can be said that whatever the allegation the private P.Ws. have made on dock implicating the accused-appellants in the occurrence is an after-thought proposition and may be treated as embellishment for obvious reason and as such no reliance can be made on the evidence of near and dear ones in this case who allegedly said about seeing the direct actions of the accused-appellants in the occurrence. More so, the wife and son of the deceased frankly admitted on dock that accused Manu Dacoit did not visit their house, but they remained meticulously silent as to how they could recognize Manu Dacoit, had he not visited their house earlier. This fact alone justify that the accused-appellants have been implicated in this case out of enmity and grudge. The independent person Wanda' kader who was allegedly residing in the P.O. house in the night of occurrence having been with-held, we find no other alternative but to hold that had he been examined in this case, would not have supported the occurrence as alleged. 

 23. Finally, the close scrutiny of the evidence of the private witnesses indicates that they, at the first instance, tried to establish that they had seen the occurrence personally, but during cross their evidence indicates that they did not see the occurrence personally but claimed to have heard the occurrence from the wife of deceased. But P.W.2 the wife of the deceased did not state that she ever reported the occurrence to other who came there just after the occurrence. In the facts and circumstances we are constrained to hold that the prosecution with ulterior motive implicated the accused-appellants inasmuch as they embellished the case stage by stage just to establish the prosecution case. On the other hand, the learned Trial Court found to have not considered the defence case, though there is evidence to the extent that the deceased was not a man of good repute and that he had connection with local dacoits. 

 24. Regard being had to the above facts and circumstances we are constrained to hold that the prosecution has hopelessly failed to prove its case and as such the impugned judgment and order of conviction cannot be supported.
